changes: Added a deterministic memory benchmark harness with core scoring, CLI handlers, registry wiring, command policy/read-only fact classification, smoke coverage, package script, and Lattice-lifecycle-memory-Evolving.md usage notes. The harness now enforces fixed 10k/100k/1M tiers, hard checks, per-metric minima, and non-authoritative benchmark boundaries.
usage: Run node bin/koala.js memory_benchmark_run --tier=T1 --format=text for a single tier, or node bin/koala.js memory_benchmark_compare --candidateCounts=10000,100000,1000000 --queryCount=120 --seed=7 --format=text for the baseline comparison. Use --format=json for machine-readable results.
expectedOutcome: A user can run a real CLI benchmark harness for memory baseline scoring and see 10k/100k/1M recall metrics, MemoryScore, hard-fail counts, thresholds, and a clear note that benchmark PASS is not Koala lifecycle gate authority.
actualTranscript: The 10k/100k/1M compare returned PASS for T1/T2/T3 with MemoryScore=100.00, exactRecall@1=1.000, recall@10=1.000, MRR@10=1.000, precision@10=1.000, hardFails=0, and the non-authority note. candidateCounts=50000 was rejected. exactRecallAt1=0.9, recallAt10=0.89, mrrAt10=0.74, and precisionAt10=0.69 each returned FAIL despite MemoryScore above threshold.
outcomeDiff: No product-facing gap: actual output matches the expected fixed-tier baseline, exposes the requested score proof, rejects unsupported tiers, and preserves the authority boundary.
limitations: The harness uses a deterministic virtual corpus and synthetic resource estimates. It proves the baseline contract and scoring mechanics, not production vector-store performance or a deployed million-candidate memory system.
pitfalls: Review found three correctness gaps that were fixed: lifecycle evidence linkage below 1 needed direct HARD_FAIL coverage, unsupported candidate counts could not be mislabeled as T3, and per-metric minima must fail independently of a high aggregate MemoryScore.
